docs.title: nyx-bridge-blender
docs.text:
Connects Blender to a running Nyx, so stages can send commands to Blender and get the results back. It is the Blender client of nyx-bridge: Blender connects out to the bridge server of Nyx, Nyx never launches or reaches into Blender on its own.

In Blender: open the 3D viewport sidebar (N), tab Nyx, press Connect to Nyx. Or from Python:

import nyx_bridge_blender

nyx_bridge_blender.start()        # connects, retrying until Nyx is up

# in blender --background
import nyx_bridge_blender

nyx_bridge_blender.BlenderClient().serve_forever()
If you want to... Read Install the extension and connect Blender to Nyx User Guide Work on nyx-bridge-blender, run its tests with bpy Developer Guide Look up a class or function API reference (see the navigation)

Requires Blender 4.2 or newer. See also nyx-bridge-maya.

docs.text:
Bases: NyxClient

Nyx client living in Blender.

What Nyx sends is run on Blender's main thread, so it can use bpy safely. Scripts find bpy, bmesh and mathutils in their namespace.

Serve from a background thread (start_in_thread, what start does) in a Blender with a window. In blender --background serve from the main thread with serve_forever: there is no event loop to hand work over to.

def run_on_main_thread(self, func: typing.Callable[[], typing.Any]) -> typing.Any:
    """Run a function on Blender's main thread and wait for its result.

    Args:
        func (Callable[[], Any]): function to run.

    Returns:
        Any: whatever the function returns.
    """
    if threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread():
        return func()
    return self._pump.submit(func)

docs.title: MainThreadPump()
docs.text:
Runs functions on the main thread of Blender for threads that need it.

Blender's Python API may only be used from the main thread. The pump lets other threads hand it a function and wait for the result: a timer of Blender, which runs on the main thread, picks the functions up (run_pending).

Initialize MainThreadPump.

Source code in src/nyx_bridge_blender/client.py 
def __init__(self) -> None:
    """Initialize MainThreadPump."""
    self._jobs: queue.Queue[_Job] = queue.Queue()
    self._active = False
    # Blender finds a timer by the identity of its function, and a bound method
    # is a new object every time it is asked for.
    self._timer = self._tick

Source code in src/nyx_bridge_blender/client.py 
def run_pending(self) -> None:
    """Run the functions that are waiting. Call it from the main thread."""
    while True:
        try:
            job = self._jobs.get_nowait()
        except queue.Empty:
            return
        if self._active:
            job.run()
        else:
            job.fail(RuntimeError("The client was stopped"))

def start(self) -> None:
    """Start taking functions and ask Blender's timers to run them.

    Call it from the main thread.
    """
    import bpy

    self._active = True
    if not bpy.app.timers.is_registered(self._timer):
        bpy.app.timers.register(self._timer, first_interval=0.0, persistent=True)

def submit(self, func: typing.Callable[[], typing.Any]) -> typing.Any:
    """Run a function on the main thread and wait for its result.

    Args:
        func (Callable[[], Any]): function to run.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: the pump is not running.

    Returns:
        Any: whatever the function returns. What it raises is raised here.
    """
    if not self._active:
        raise RuntimeError("Nothing runs functions on the main thread of Blender")
    job = _Job(func)
    self._jobs.put(job)
    job.done.wait()
    if job.error is not None:
        raise job.error
    return job.result

docs.title: serve_background(name=None, address=None, token=None, connect_timeout=None)
docs.text:
Serve Nyx from the main thread of a Blender running with --background.

There is no event loop to hand work to, so the requests run right on the calling thread. Returns when Nyx asks the client to shut down or the connection ends, it does not reconnect, and Blender then exits as its script is done. Start it from a Launch Process node of Nyx with a command like

blender --background --python-expr "import nyx_bridge_blender;
nyx_bridge_blender.serve_background()"

The extension has to be installed and enabled for the package to be importable.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default name str | None

name Nyx shows for this Blender, NYX_BRIDGE_CLIENT_NAME if omitted, then derived from the process id.

None address str | tuple[str, int] | None

host:port of Nyx, see start.

None token str | None

token of the Nyx server.

None connect_timeout float | None

seconds to keep trying to reach Nyx, forever if omitted.

None Source code in src/nyx_bridge_blender/client.py 
def serve_background(
    name: str | None = None,
    address: str | tuple[str, int] | None = None,
    token: str | None = None,
    connect_timeout: float | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Serve Nyx from the main thread of a Blender running with `--background`.

    There is no event loop to hand work to, so the requests run right on the calling
    thread. Returns when Nyx asks the client to shut down or the connection ends, it
    does not reconnect, and Blender then exits as its script is done. Start it from a
    Launch Process node of Nyx with a command like

        blender --background --python-expr "import nyx_bridge_blender;
        nyx_bridge_blender.serve_background()"

    The extension has to be installed and enabled for the package to be importable.

    Args:
        name (str | None): name Nyx shows for this Blender, `NYX_BRIDGE_CLIENT_NAME` if
            omitted, then derived from the process id.
        address (str | tuple[str, int] | None): `host:port` of Nyx, see `start`.
        token (str | None): token of the Nyx server.
        connect_timeout (float | None): seconds to keep trying to reach Nyx, forever if
            omitted.
    """
    BlenderClient(
        name=name or os.environ.get(CLIENT_NAME_VARIABLE) or None,
        address=address,
        token=token,
        reconnect=False,
    ).serve_forever(connect_timeout)

docs.text:
Connect Blender to Nyx from a background thread, and keep trying until it works.

Where Nyx is comes from the arguments, then the environment, then the address file Nyx writes, see nyx_bridge.protocol.find_server_address. It does not matter whether Nyx is already running: the client connects once it is, and again if the connection drops. Call it from the main thread.

token of the Nyx server.

Returns:

Name Type Description BlenderClient BlenderClient

the running client. An already running one is returned as it is, the arguments are ignored.

Source code in src/nyx_bridge_blender/client.py 
def start(
    address: str | tuple[str, int] | None = None,
    token: str | None = None,
    name: str | None = None,
) -> BlenderClient:
    """Connect Blender to Nyx from a background thread, and keep trying until it works.

    Where Nyx is comes from the arguments, then the environment, then the address file
    Nyx writes, see `nyx_bridge.protocol.find_server_address`. It does not matter
    whether Nyx is already running: the client connects once it is, and again if
    the connection drops. Call it from the main thread.

    Args:
        address (str | tuple[str, int] | None): `host:port` of Nyx.
        token (str | None): token of the Nyx server.
        name (str | None): name Nyx shows for this Blender. Derived from the process id
            if omitted.

    Returns:
        BlenderClient: the running client. An already running one is returned as it
            is, the arguments are ignored.
    """
    global _client, _thread
    if is_running():
        return _client
    _client = BlenderClient(name=name, address=address, token=token)
    _thread = _client.start_in_thread()
    return _client

docs.title: stop()
docs.text:
Disconnect from Nyx and stop the client started by start.

Source code in src/nyx_bridge_blender/client.py 
def stop() -> None:
    """Disconnect from Nyx and stop the client started by `start`."""
    global _client, _thread
    client, thread = _client, _thread
    _client = _thread = None
    if client is not None:
        client.stop()
    if thread is not None and thread is not threading.current_thread():
        thread.join(timeout=5)

    if is_running():
        return _client
    _client = BlenderClient(name=name, address=address, token=token)
    _thread = _client.start_in_thread()
    return _client

docs.title: stop()
docs.text:
Disconnect from Nyx and stop the client started by start.

Source code in src/nyx_bridge_blender/client.py 
def stop() -> None:
    """Disconnect from Nyx and stop the client started by `start`."""
    global _client, _thread
    client, thread = _client, _thread
    _client = _thread = None
    if client is not None:
        client.stop()
    if thread is not None and thread is not threading.current_thread():
        thread.join(timeout=5)

docs.title: Developer Guide
docs.text: This guide is for people who work on nyx-bridge-blender itself.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
uv sync
make check        # ruff + pytest with bpy
make mkdocs       # serve these docs

make help lists every target. Ruff uses a line length of 89 and the E, F and UP rules. Docstrings are Google style: the API reference is generated from them.

Tests do not need a Blender install: they use the bpy package. See Testing.

Important

import nyx_bridge_blender must work outside Blender (docs, tooling), so bpy, bmesh and mathutils are imported inside the methods that use them. Only the modules of extension/ import bpy at the top, since Blender is the only one loading them.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: Page What you learn Architecture The package, the extension, threads and the main-thread pump. Testing The bpy package, the test layout and CI. Releasing Versions, the changelog and make release. API reference Generated from the docstrings (see the navigation).

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
src
└── nyx_bridge_blender
    ├── client.py    BlenderClient, MainThreadPump, start/stop/is_*, serve_background
    └── version.py   __version__
extension
├── __init__.py             register / unregister, connect on start
├── blender_manifest.toml   the extension manifest
├── operators.py            nyx.connect, nyx.disconnect
├── panel.py                sidebar panel and its redraw timer
└── preferences.py          address, token, name, connect on start
scripts/build_extension.py  assembles and builds the zip

BlenderClient is a subclass of nyx_bridge.client.NyxClient; see Writing a client for what each hook is.

Member Blender specific CLIENT_KIND "blender" client_version() bpy.app.version_string default_namespace() bpy, bmesh, mathutils run_on_main_thread(func) Runs func directly on the main thread, else hands it to the MainThreadPump. start_in_thread() / stop() Also start and stop the pump.

docs.title: Two ways to serve
docs.text:
• Blender with a window: start() uses start_in_thread(). The reading loop lives on a daemon thread, and every execution is handed to the main thread through the pump.
  • blender --background: there is no event loop to run timers, so handing work over would wait forever. serve_background() serves from the main thread with serve_forever(), where run_on_main_thread calls func straight away. reconnect=False, since the process is started for one stage.

docs.title: The main-thread pump
docs.text:
Blender's API may only be used from the main thread, and has no executeInMainThread. MainThreadPump fills that gap:

  1. A worker thread calls submit(func), which queues a job and waits on its event.
  2. A timer registered with bpy.app.timers (every INTERVAL, 20 ms) calls run_pending() on the main thread, which runs the jobs and wakes the waiters with the result or the exception.
  3. stop() makes the timer return None (removing it) and fails the jobs still waiting, so no thread hangs on a stopped client.

The timer function is stored once (self._timer): Blender finds a timer by the identity of its function, and a bound method is a new object every time it is asked for. The timer is persistent, so it survives loading another file.

start_in_thread() must be called from the main thread, since that is where the timer is registered.

docs.title: Module state
docs.text: client.py keeps one client and its thread in module globals. start() returns the running one, stop() clears them and joins the thread (5 s). The extension's unregister calls stop(), so disabling it never leaves a connection behind.

docs.title: The extension
docs.text: register() adds the preferences, the two operators and the panel, starts the redraw timer (1 s, so the panel follows the connection) and, after AUTO_CONNECT_DELAY, a timer that connects when Connect on start is on. connection_arguments() turns the preferences into the arguments of start(), None for empty fields. get_preferences() returns None while the extension is not enabled as an add-on, as in tests.

docs.title: The zip
docs.text:
scripts/build_extension.py copies extension/ into build/extension/, builds a wheel of the package and of every dependency into its wheels/ folder, writes the list into blender_manifest.toml (at the line # The wheels are added by ...), and has Blender pack it (blender --command extension build). Dependencies are built from the git revision pinned in [tool.uv.sources] if it has one, otherwise downloaded from the package index. The set of dependencies and their versions come from uv export, so they match uv.lock, and they must be pure Python wheels. The manifest version must equal VERSION, or the build stops.

The targets come from sowwic/makefiles (dcc/blender), fetched into .make/ and committed; make update-make fetches them again.

docs.title: Branches and versions
docs.text:
develop is the default and PR branch; main is the release branch. Work on a feature branch named after the GitHub issue (3-update-nyx-bridge-dependency).

The version lives in VERSION. make update-version copies it into pyproject.toml; extension/blender_manifest.toml has its own version that must be kept equal, or make extension stops. Add a v<version> section at the top of CHANGELOG.rst, one bullet per user-visible change with the issue number where there is one.

nyx-bridge-blender depends on sowwic-nyx-bridge. When a new nyx-bridge release is needed, raise the minimum in pyproject.toml, run uv lock and add a changelog bullet. The extension zip bundles the version uv.lock holds.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
1. Update CHANGELOG.rst, VERSION (make update-version) and the manifest version, commit on main.
  2. Run
make release VERSION=1.2.3 [RELEASE_TITLE="..."]

It tags main, pushes and merges back into develop. The tag triggers .github/workflows/release.yml, which creates the GitHub release from the changelog section.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: Workflows in .github/workflows/ are thin callers of the shared ones in sowwic/gh-workflows: tests (see Testing), lint, docs deployment to GitHub Pages and the release. Dependabot opens update PRs against develop.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
The tests run with the bpy package, Blender as a Python module, so no Blender install is needed.

make pytest                                  # everything, with coverage
uv run --group bpy pytest tests -k pump      # a selection
make pytest-pdb                              # verbose, pdb on failure

docs.title: Setting up
docs.text:
bpy is a 250 MB download the first time. Each bpy release needs exactly one Python version: 5.2 needs 3.13 (see .python-version), and has no wheel for Intel Macs or Linux on ARM. It is in its own dependency group, bpy, which the make targets add: uv sync alone leaves it out, and does not stop the rest of the project from working.

A plain pytest without bpy skips everything but test_package.py (see pytest_collection_modifyitems in tests/conftest.py), so lint and docs jobs need no Blender. make validate checks the extension manifest, which does need a Blender (BLENDER in .env, see Installation).

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
File Covers tests/test_package.py The package imports (runs without bpy). tests/test_pump.py MainThreadPump: results, errors, order, stopping, the timer; the client's choice between direct call and pump. tests/test_client.py BlenderClient against a real BridgeServer over loopback: description, namespace, errors. tests/test_start_stop.py start/stop, waiting for Nyx to appear, serve_background. tests/test_extension.py The extension loaded from extension/: registering, operators, preferences, connect on start.

tests/conftest.py provides output_dir.

docs.title: Fixtures and helpers
docs.text:
• server (BridgeServer(port=0)): the system picks a free port, so tests can run while Nyx is open.
  • make_client(server, **kwargs) (test_client.py): a BlenderClient pointed at that server with reconnect=False.
  • run_remote(server, client, *requests) (test_client.py): the client serves on the main thread, as in blender --background, while another thread sends the requests and collects results.
  • pump and serve_until_done(pump, thread) (test_pump.py): the test acts as Blender's timer, calling run_pending() on the main thread while a thread waits.
  • extension (test_extension.py): loads extension/ from its folder under a throwaway package name, registers it, and unregisters after.
  • wait_until(predicate, timeout=15) (test_extension.py): poll instead of sleep.

docs.title: What to cover
docs.text:
• A new preference or operator: a test in test_extension.py going through the registered classes.
  • Anything that depends on threads: keep timeouts generous (10 to 15 s) and wait on conditions. A flaky test here is almost always a missing wait.
  • Behavior that needs Blender's real event loop (the timer firing in a window) can't run with bpy as a module; test the pump through run_pending() and check an interactive Blender when a change touches the main-thread hand-off.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: .github/workflows/unit_tests.yml calls the shared python-tests workflow on hosted runners with Python 3.13 and the libraries Blender loads (libegl1, libgl1, ...). It runs uv run --group bpy pytest tests. Lint (code_quality.yml) needs no Blender: make lint.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: This guide is for people who connect Blender to Nyx.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: Page What you learn Installation Building and installing the Blender extension, checking that Blender has it. Connecting Blender to Nyx The sidebar panel, the preferences, the Python API, addresses and tokens, what scripts see. Starting Blender from a stage Headless blender --background started by a Launch Process node.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
Nyx                                       Blender
┌──────────────┐ Blender connects out   ┌───────────────────┐
│ BridgeServer │ ◀───────────────────── │ BlenderClient     │
│              │ ───── execute ───────▶ │ runs on the main  │
│ ClientSession│ ◀──── result ───────── │ thread            │
└──────────────┘                        └───────────────────┘
  1. Nyx listens on a local port and holds a secret token.
  2. Blender starts a BlenderClient (with the Connect to Nyx button or nyx_bridge_blender.start()), which keeps trying until Nyx accepts it.
  3. Nyx sends code; Blender runs it on its main thread and answers with the value and the captured output.

Protocol and server details are in the nyx-bridge documentation.

docs.title: Starting Blender from a stage
docs.text:
A stage can start a headless Blender itself, wait for it to connect and run its Remote Actions in it. Use a Launch Process node around a Remote Client:

Launch Process  ->  Remote Client  ->  Remote Action ...

Settings of the Launch Process node:

Input Value command "$BLENDER" --background --python-exit-code 1 --python-expr "import nyx_bridge_blender; nyx_bridge_blender.serve_background()" env {"BLENDER": "/Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender"} timeout Seconds to wait for Blender to boot (default 60).

Nyx gives the process the address and token of its bridge server and the name it is to connect as (NYX_BRIDGE_ADDRESS, NYX_BRIDGE_TOKEN, NYX_BRIDGE_CLIENT_NAME), which serve_background uses. The Remote Client inside the node uses that Blender and no other.

  • The extension has to be installed: Blender loads it from the user preferences, so do not start with --factory-startup.
  • blender --background has no event loop, so requests run on the calling thread and serve_background does not reconnect: it returns when Nyx asks Blender to shut down or the connection ends, and Blender exits as its script is done.
  • --python-exit-code 1 makes Blender's exit code say that the script failed.
  • When the nodes inside are done Nyx asks Blender to shut down, and stops the process if it does not. The Nyx window waits while Blender boots.
  • A small launcher script holding the command makes the node's command just its path.

docs.title: Without Nyx starting it
docs.text:
In your own blender --background script:

from nyx_bridge_blender import BlenderClient

BlenderClient().serve_forever()     # blocks; address from the environment or address file

serve_background(name, address, token, connect_timeout) takes the same settings. Give connect_timeout (seconds) to fail with ConnectionError instead of waiting forever.

docs.title: Connecting Blender to Nyx
docs.text: Once the extension is installed, Blender connects to Nyx in one of three ways. All of them start a BlenderClient, which keeps retrying until Nyx is running, and connects again if the connection drops.

docs.title: The sidebar panel
docs.text:
In the 3D viewport sidebar (N), tab Nyx:

State shown Meaning Not connected No client. Press Connect to Nyx. Waiting for Nyx... The client runs and keeps trying. Disconnect from Nyx stops it. Connected to server Nyx accepted Blender, shown with the name it uses.

The panel redraws once a second, so it follows the connection by itself. Disabling the extension disconnects.

docs.title: Preferences
docs.text:
Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > Nyx Bridge:

Setting Meaning Connect on start Connect when Blender starts or the extension is enabled (after a second, once the preferences are loaded). Off by default. Address host:port of Nyx. Empty finds a Nyx running on this computer. Token Token of the Nyx server. Empty uses the one Nyx wrote or the environment. Name Name Nyx shows for this Blender. Empty uses the process id.

The button and Connect on start use these settings.

docs.title: From Python
docs.text:
Without the panel:

import nyx_bridge_blender

nyx_bridge_blender.start()                      # background thread, returns the client
nyx_bridge_blender.is_running()                 # serving, connected or not
nyx_bridge_blender.is_connected()
nyx_bridge_blender.get_client()                 # the BlenderClient, None if not started
nyx_bridge_blender.stop()

start(address=None, token=None, name=None) returns the already running client if there is one and ignores its arguments then. Call it from Blender's main thread.

docs.title: Finding Nyx
docs.text:
Blender looks for the host, port and token in this order:

  1. The address and token arguments (the Address and Token preferences).
  2. The environment: NYX_BRIDGE_ADDRESS (host:port) with NYX_BRIDGE_TOKEN.
  3. The address file a running Nyx writes.

On the same machine nothing needs to be configured. For Nyx on another machine give host:port and the token. Details are in Finding the server.

Blender then shows up in Nyx's Bridge panel as a client of kind blender, and the Remote Client and Remote Action nodes can use it.

docs.title: What scripts see
docs.text:
What Nyx sends runs on Blender's main thread, so bpy is safe to use. The namespace of a connection lives as long as the connection, and starts with:

Name Is bpy bpy bmesh bmesh mathutils mathutils 
# what a stage sends
result = bpy.data.objects["Cube"].name

Printed output is sent back, an exception comes back as an error of that execution and Blender keeps working. Executions run one at a time, handed to the main thread by a timer every 20 ms at most: while a long script runs, Blender's UI is busy as with any script run in the Text Editor.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Connections are logged to nyx_bridge_blender.client (and nyx_bridge.client) at INFO.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: nyx-bridge-blender is installed as a Blender extension: a zip holding the add-on and the wheels of the Python packages it needs (this package and nyx-bridge), so nothing is installed into Blender's own Python and nothing is downloaded when Blender installs it.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Blender 4.2 or newer.
  • uv, make and git, to build the extension from source.

docs.title: 1. Tell the build where Blender is
docs.text:
Create a .env file in the project root (or ~/.config/blender-ci.env):

BLENDER=/Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender
Variable Meaning BLENDER The Blender executable. Used to build the zip, validate the manifest and install.

Typical locations:

Platform Executable macOS /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender Windows C:\Program Files\Blender Foundation\Blender 4.2\blender.exe Linux /usr/bin/blender, or where you unpacked Blender

The file is looked up in this order: BLENDER_CI_ENV_FILE, ./.env, ~/.config/blender-ci.env.

docs.title: 2. Install
docs.text:
make install

This runs two steps you can also run alone:

Target What it does make extension Builds dist/nyx_bridge_blender-<version>.zip: wheels of this package and of sowwic-nyx-bridge (at the version in uv.lock, downloaded from the package index) plus the extension, packed by Blender. make install Builds the zip, then installs it in the user_default repository and enables it.

To remove it: make uninstall. make validate checks extension/blender_manifest.toml with Blender.

docs.title: Without make
docs.text: Build the zip with make extension, then in Blender use Edit > Preferences > Get Extensions, the arrow menu (top right) and Install from Disk. Blender keeps installed extensions in its user folder, for example ~/Library/Application Support/Blender/<version>/extensions/user_default/.

docs.title: 3. Check it in Blender
docs.text:
Open the 3D viewport sidebar (N): there is a Nyx tab. In the Python Console:

import nyx_bridge_blender
print(nyx_bridge_blender.__version__)

The extension asks for the network permission ("Connect to Nyx on this computer"), which Blender shows in the extension's entry.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Check Set BLENDER in ... The env file is missing or does not define BLENDER. blender_manifest.toml is at version X, VERSION says Y Run make update-version. Not pure Python, so not bundled: ... A dependency in uv.lock only has platform specific wheels. One zip serves every platform, so only py3-none-any wheels can be bundled. No Nyx tab in the sidebar The extension is not enabled: Edit > Preferences > Add-ons. No module named nyx_bridge_blender Installed some other way than as the extension zip, which carries the wheels. Old behavior after pulling changes Run make install again.
